text:
Nadia: quick note from overnight bring-up of pandora-ptq (new PTQ variant) against the structured-invoke harness. We're seeing a weird class of failures I'm calling 'stitch-breaks' (~1.9%): the model emits valid JSON fragments that only become valid when stitched together, or emits interleaved prose between fragments. Parser treats each fragment independently and fails.

Ravi: can you paste a raw capture?

Nadia: sure, harness captured this stream:
```
{
  "action": "open_ticket",
  "params": {"title": "Login failing for
```
(then later in the same response)
```
user-123"}
}
```
If you naively parse per-fragment you get two invalid objects; concatenated they form a valid one. Other hits have a short sentence between fragments: "bridging note: see below" sandwiched in the middle of the JSON.

Ellen: interesting. So it's not trailing commas or fences, it's mid-object fragmentation. That smells like quantized logits causing stop/emit patterns mid-structure.

Ravi: two immediate heuristic ideas: 1) stitch-healer: buffer adjacent non-parseable fragments within the same response and attempt concat+parse up to a limit (e.g., 4 fragments / 512 chars); 2) prose-clip: if there's short natural language between fragments, drop it and attempt stitching. Both risky (could fuse unrelated objects).

Nadia: I prototyped a stitcher that only stitches when the concatenated candidate contains all required top-level keys and no duplicate keys. It also rejects if the combined length grows >2x prompt length. Quick local run reduced stitch-breaks from 1.9% -> 0.45% but introduced a small false-stitch rate (~0.11%) where we accidentally combined two separate actions into one.

Ellen: what's the semantic impact on actions? Are we changing the intended tool or params?

Nadia: measured semantic_match where the action key equals the golden action: stitch branch had 99.3% semantic match vs baseline 99.1% (slight improvement), but the false-stitch cases were catastrophic (wrong combined params). We need guardrails: only stitch when required fields are present and types align, and sample fused cases.

Ravi: propose an ABX design over 8k calls: A = baseline (no stitch), B = conservative stitch (stitch only if required keys present and single occurrence), C = stitch + retry (temp=0.0, system: "output only JSON, no commentary", max_new_tokens=64), D = stitch + kvcache_strip=recent_only (to test long-context interference). Track parse_success, semantic_match, false_stitch_rate, p50/p95 latency, tokens delta. Also mark any fused calls where the final object includes combined arrays/merged params for manual triage.

Ellen: add another tiny probe: decoder-logit tweak where we slightly boost brace tokens 1.1x and penalize common prose tokens like "see", "note" to see if we can reduce prose insertions. Run 1k sample to ensure no regressions.

ops-bot: scheduled job: "pandora-ptq-stitch-ab-8k" - queued :rocket:

stability-bot: run created id=run-20260323-pandora-ptq-stitch ; ETA ~40m :hourglass:

Ravi: also track context-length split (single-turn vs 3-turn) and whether the prompt included an explicit system instruction to only respond with JSON. That correlates with stitch incidence in my earlier runs.

Nadia: timeline: I'll collect run results, example fused cases, and a short doc with stitch heuristics + thresholds by EOD tomorrow. If B or C reduces failures <0.3% with false_stitch <0.08% and acceptable latency, we can consider enabling as a runtime fallback behind a flag for dedicated customers.

Ellen: please include cost delta and sample counts for manual triage. I'll help label fused cases tomorrow morning.

Nadia: thanks all. Also added a note to log character offsets of fragments so we can debug whether kv-cache truncation correlates. :coffee:
